data.segment_title: Economy: Crisis, Stock Market / Sonders Interview / Overseas
data.segment_description:
(Davenport, Iowa: Charles Gibson)  The drop in the stock market this week reviewed with graphs shown.  

(Studio: Betsy Stark)  A harrowing week in global financial markets reviewed; scenes shown from the floor of the New York Stock Exchange; details given of the wave of selling each day of the week and about the loss of trillions in investment in two weeks.  [Jefferies and Co. strategist Art HOGAN†- comments.]  [President BUSH&nbsp- says we can solve this crisis.]  [Moody's economy.com economist Mark ZANDI†- says people need proof these things will work; states savings have vanished.]  [Johnson Illington Advisors CEO Hugh JOHNSON†- comments on the market going up and down.]  Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson's confirmation the Treasury Department will take part ownership of some US banks to stabilize financial institutions noted.  

(Davenport, Iowa: Charles Gibson)  Earlier discussion held with Charles Schwab investment strategist Liz Ann Sonders† about the market.  [SONDERS&nbsp- assesses this remarkable day on the Friday market; calls it "unprecedented volatility"; asserts we are going through a pervasive time of fear; suggests the recovery of the market and the economy will happen over time.]  

(New York: Bianna Golodryga)  The view from the floor of the stock market presented; scenes shown.  [Trader Jason WEISBERG‡- offers his views on what is happening.]  [In Reston, Virginia, Baird Financial Advisors Randy BEEMAN†- outlines the questions about retirement assets.]  

(Davenport, Iowa: Charles Gibson)  A calamitous day in the world markets reviewed; statistics from the markets in Japan, Australia and Britain cited; scenes shown of Paulson meeting with finance ministers.  

(London: Jim Sciutto)  The reverberation around the globe of the financial crisis featured; details given about Iceland's debt, concerns about a European recession and production cutbacks by several companies in Europe and China.  [Cantor Fitzgerald global market strategist Stephen POPE†- says there is a breakdown of trust among European banks.]  [World bank president Robert ZOELLICK†- comments on the situation for the US and overseas.]

(Dixon, Illinois, Eldridge and Bettendorf, Iowa: Charles Gibson)  The view of the economy from Main Street in the Midwest presented; scenes shown from President Ronald Reagan's hometown of Dixon, Illinois, a cornfield in Eldridge, Iowa and a diner in Bettendorf, Iowa.  [Dixon broker Kim PETTIGROVE††- offers advice.]  [In a local book store, retirees Marilyn and Tom COFFEY†- react to the financial situation.]  [Iowa farmer Neal KEPPY††- says the price of corn is most volatile; questions the government bailout.]  [In Iowa diner, ownersRon FRIEDHOF††, customers Jackie JOHNSON††, Diane NELSON††- talk about the economy.]

Campaign 2008 / Obama vs. McCain / The Trail
data.segment_description: (Davenport, Iowa: Charles Gibson)  Report introduced.   (Lakeville, Minnesota: David Wright)  Senator John McCain's campaigning against Senator Barack Obama's record and character featured; TV ad shown; details given about his campaign to refinance mortgages and to allow seniors to delay cashing out their IRAs.  [In La Crosse, Wisconsin and Lakeville, Minnesota, McCAIN&nbsp- campaigns against Obama and on change; outlines a plan to spare investors.]  [Voters Lynn MARTALOCK†, Todd RUHBUSCH†- offer their views on the two candidates.]   (Columbus, Ohio: John Berman)  Obama's campaigning on the financial crisis and on political angles about McCain featured; details given about his new policies of loans to small businesses.  [In Chillicothe†† and Columbus, Ohio, OBAMA&nbsp- campaigns on the economy; calls for people to believe in the future.]  [VOTER&nbsp- responds.]  The thrust of Obama's new campaign ad quoted.
